title: Kazakhstan approves up to 10 years of power support for crypto miners
summary: Kazakhstan has approved rules for a strategic digital mining program that guarantee electricity supplies to cryptocurrency mining companies for up to 10 years, according to a report by a West Asian media outlet. Under the rules, participating companies can receive power allocations from electricity generators at capped rates. In return, they must transfer part of their mined cryptocurrency to Kazakhstan’s Silicon Valley, Astar Network, or a hub, and the assets will be held in trust by a state investment corporation under the central bank before being used to expand the country’s strategic crypto reserve.

title: South Korean lawmaker urges swift stablecoin bill as U.S. CLARITY Act nears vote
summary: South Korean Rep. Kim Hyun-jung of the Democratic Party called for swift passage of a second-phase digital asset bill covering won-denominated stablecoins at a conference held at the National Assembly Members' Office Building on July 23, Edaily reported. Kim said South Korea needs to prepare as broader dollar stablecoin adoption is expected after the GENIUS Act takes full effect in January next year and the U.S. market structure bill, the CLARITY Act, could come to a vote as early as next week.At the same event, when asked whether the government’s digital asset basic law on stablecoins would be released in the second half of the year, Kim Sung-jin, head of the virtual asset division at South Korea’s Financial Services Commission, said the schedule remains under discussion with relevant agencies and the National Assembly and that officials are working to move as quickly as possible, as outlined in the government’s economic policy direction for the second half. more:

title: Institutional BTC demand slows across ETFs, Strategy and accumulation firms
summary: On-chain analyst Darkfost said demand from spot Bitcoin ETFs, Strategy and corporate Bitcoin accumulation firms is all slowing. In a post on X, Darkfost said net inflows into spot ETFs over the past 30 days fell by $2.1 billion, while Strategy's purchase demand has stagnated for weeks. Demand from accumulation firms has also dropped from about $6.6 billion in August last year to effectively near zero now. Darkfost said the trend reflects market pessimism, but added that periods when demand from those buyers is at its lowest could instead offer a good time to build positions.

summary: Former U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Christopher Giancarlo sees the CLARITY bill as having less than a 50% chance of passing, Crypto in America host Eleanor Terrett said on X.
